one_liner: Closed-source lossless RGB/gray image codec (CLI binaries) that encodes about 15-32x faster than Pillow PNG and WebP lossless at smaller size.
what_it_does: HALIC is a pair of command-line programs (encoder and decoder) that losslessly compress 8-bit RGB PPM/PNM images, and gray PGM from 0.7.2 on, into its own .halic format. Usage is 'HALIC072e.exe in.pnm out.halic' and 'HALIC072d.exe in.halic out.pnm'; there is no library, header, API or format specification, only Windows .exe and static Linux x64 executables attached to GitHub releases. It replaces a PNG or WebP-lossless archive step in a pipeline only if you can keep a private, undocumented format and the vendor's binaries.
how_it_is_fast: Per the README: simple prediction without context modelling or error correction, so many residuals remain, followed by an ANS entropy coder (FSE) over completely independent blocks and per-channel sub-streams; the measured build runs on one thread. Skipping context mixing is what keeps it near QOI-class speed while compressing close to WebP lossless. The predictor, block size and any SIMD use are not documented: the README says no SIMD or assembly, yet the 0.7.2 assets are labelled AVX and AVX2 builds (compiler target flags, presumably).
when_to_use: Batch archiving of large 24-bit photographs (multi-megapixel PPM/PNM) where encode time dominates: on CLIC2021 it encoded 4.1 GB in 22.2 s versus 334.8 s for Pillow PNG and 720.2 s for Pillow WebP lossless m1, with output 26% smaller than that PNG.
Research or comparison work that needs a fast-symmetric reference point between QOI/QOIR-class speed and WebP-lossless-class size.
Closed environments (offline tools, internal storage) on x86-64 Windows or Linux where running a third-party binary is acceptable and interoperability with other software is not needed.
when_not_to_use: Anything that must be built, audited, fuzzed or embedded: there is no source in the repo, releases or the author's HALIC-Image-Converter, despite the MIT LICENSE file.
Interchange or long-term storage: .halic is undocumented, single-vendor, and the project has had no release since 0.7.2 (March 2024) or commit since May 2024.

Small images: process start-up per file dominates, and on UCID (1338 small images) HALIC decoded in 27.2 s versus 15.0 s for WebP lossless m1 and 15.2 s for Pillow PNG; on Kodak Pillow PNG decoded faster too (0.484 s versus 0.615 s).
Best ratio: JPEG XL e3 and up, fNBLI, BMF, EMMA and other context-mixing codecs are 5-17% smaller on CLIC2021.
Alpha channels, 16-bit samples, PNG input or other non-PNM formats: not supported or not documented.

integration.form: prebuilt command-line executables only (no library, no source)
integration.dependencies: none at run time (Linux builds are static)
integration.min_toolchain: not applicable (no source); 0.7.2 Windows builds need an x86-64 CPU with AVX or AVX2, Linux builds AVX2
integration.platforms: Windows x64 (.exe, AVX and AVX2 variants), Linux x64 static (AVX2); release 0.6.0 also shipped Windows ARM64 executables
integration.thread_safety: not applicable (separate processes); 0.7.2 assets are all single-threaded 'ST' builds, 0.7.0 also had a multithreaded encoder (HALIC_ENCODE_V.0.7.0_MT.exe)

gotchas: The 'FAST' variant (HALIC072fe/fd) is labelled trial in the 0.7.2 notes and failed to decompress zone_plate.pnm in the ImgInfoGray set of the benchmark.

The benchmark's published RunBenchmark.py has CHECK_DISTORTION = False, so the run as published does not compare decoded pixels with the input; only non-zero exit codes are caught, which is how the FAST failure surfaced.
The GitHub 'Source code' archives on each release are only the README-only tree; the codec itself is closed.
The format has no spec or version-compatibility statement; keep the exact decoder binary that wrote your files.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick HALIC over fNBLI (GPL-3.0 source, 9% smaller and about as fast to decode on CLIC2021, but 43.2 s versus 22.2 s to encode) only when encode speed matters more than having code; pick Zpng (BSD-3-Clause) or QOIR (Apache-2.0) when you need embeddable source at similar speed and can accept 19-45% larger files than HALIC.
verified_claims_summary: In WangXuan95's Image-Compression-Benchmark (Intel Core i7-12700H, Windows 10, every codec single-threaded, timed with time.time() over the whole set), HALIC 0.7.2 .exe compressed CLIC2021 (585 RGB images, 4.1 GB) to 1,473,481,803 bytes in 22.187 s and decompressed it in 28.447 s, versus Pillow 10.1.0 WebP lossless method 1 at 1,496,478,650 bytes, 720.160 s and 37.044 s, and Pillow PNG optimize=False (zlib default level; Pillow 10.1.0's Windows build script pins libwebp 1.3.2 and zlib 1.3) at 2,003,016,524 bytes, 334.791 s and 33.677 s; on GDCC2020 it took 4.780 s and 5.426 s versus PNG at 152.321 s and 11.545 s. The WebP baseline ran at quality=100, which in libwebp lossless mode means maximum compression effort, so the 32x encode gap is against a slow WebP setting, while HALIC's times include one process launch per image and the Pillow codecs ran in-process.
status_note: Stale since 2024-05-24 (LICENSE added; last binaries 0.7.2 from 2024-03-13, no issues filed) and reference-only: the MIT licence covers a README, not inspectable code, so treat it as a benchmark point rather than something to ship.
